title: 5 Years of Product Hunt: Ryan Hoover's lessons on building a startup
summary: Ryan Hoover reflects on five years of building Product Hunt, sharing the mistakes and learnings from running a venture-backed company. Topics include org structure, repeating your mission, hiring, distributed teams, avoiding pointless redesigns, and planning for fundraising and acquisition early.

principles.text: Some structure and clear ownership beats a fully flat org; flatness can backfire.
principles.quote: For years Product Hunt had a very flat structure, driven by my desire to encourage autonomy and a culture of mutual respect across the org. But this lack of structure and clear areas of ownership resulted in the opposite effect.

principles.text: Over-communicate mission and strategy; if teammates ask what and why, it's the founder's failure.
principles.quote: I did a poor job of communicating our mission and strategy clearly and frequently to my teammates that are often heads down on a very specific part of the business.

principles.text: A founder's words carry outsized weight, so choose them carefully.
principles.quote: The ideas a founder promotes or shoots down can dramatically shift the team’s focus and motivation, for better or worse.

principles.text: Hiring the wrong people can sink a startup; fit depends on product, culture and stage.
principles.quote: Sometimes it’s simply not the right fit for the product, culture, or stage of the company at that time.

principles.text: Distributed teams unlock global talent, but may not work for everyone or at large scale.
principles.quote: This has enabled us to hire amazing talent from anywhere in the world, not just the <1% that live in or can relocate to San Francisco.

principles.text: Skip cosmetic redesigns unless they change user behavior or metrics.
principles.quote: Don’t let your ego get in the way of prioritizing what’s right for the business and your users.
